learn.hook: An auto fare of ₹30 plus ₹15 for every km grows by the same amount each km. That steady growth is a linear polynomial!
points: A linear polynomial in x has the form ax + b, where a and b are numbers and a ≠ 0.
Its degree is 1: the highest power of x is x¹. Terms like x², 1/x or √x are not allowed.
a is the coefficient of x and b is the constant term.
To evaluate p(x) at x = k, replace x by k: p(k) = ak + b.
Each time x goes up by 1, the value of ax + b changes by exactly a.

example.q: A taxi charges ₹50 to start plus ₹12 per km. Write the fare for x km as a polynomial and find the fare for 8 km.

learn.reallife: Electricity bills, mobile data plans and taxi fares often have a fixed charge plus a charge per unit: a linear polynomial.

items.text: In 7x − 3, the coefficient of x is ___
The degree of a linear polynomial is ___

quiz.q: Which of these is a linear polynomial?
quiz.explain: 4x − 1 has the form ax + b with highest power of x equal to 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any expression with x is linear, even with x², x³ or x in the denominator

quiz.q: If p(x) = 3x − 7, find p(4).
quiz.explain: Replace x by 4 and simplify.
quiz.mistake: Adds 7 instead of subtracting it, getting 19

quiz.q: What is the degree of the polynomial 6 − 2x?
quiz.explain: The highest power of x is x¹, so the degree is 1.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the degree with a coefficient or the constant term

quiz.q: Aisha's phone plan costs ₹99 fixed plus ₹2 per GB of data. Which polynomial gives the cost for x GB?
quiz.explain: The ₹2 is paid for each GB, so it multiplies x. The ₹99 is paid once, so it is the constant.
quiz.mistake: Attaches x to the fixed charge instead of the per-unit charge

quiz.q: For p(x) = 5x + 2, find p(−3).
quiz.mistake: Drops the negative sign when multiplying by −3

quiz.q: At a sports shop the price of x cricket balls is p(x) = 150x rupees. What is p(4) − p(3)?
quiz.explain: One extra ball adds the coefficient of x, ₹150, to the price.
quiz.mistake: Gives p(4) or p(3) instead of their difference

quiz.q: Which expression is NOT a linear polynomial?
quiz.explain: x(x + 1) = x² + x has degree 2, so it is not linear. x/3 + 1 is linear because x/3 = (1/3)x.
quiz.mistake: Thinks dividing x by a number makes it non-linear, or misses the hidden x²

quiz.q: If p(x) = ax + 4 and p(2) = 10, what is a?
quiz.explain: Put x = 2: 2a + 4 = 10, so 2a = 6 and a = 3.
quiz.mistake: Divides 10 by 2 without first subtracting 4

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What makes a polynomial 'linear'? It sounds like a line, but it is just letters and numbers!"
teach.praise: Highest power of x is one, like ax + b. And it really does make a line on a graph. Super!
teach.nudge: What is the highest power of x allowed in a linear polynomial?

learn.hook: Put a linear polynomial on a graph and something magical happens: every point falls in one perfectly straight line!
points: To graph y = ax + b, make a table: choose some x-values, work out y, plot the points (x, y) and join them.
The graph of a linear polynomial is always a straight line. Two points are enough to draw it; a third point is a good check.
b is where the line cuts the y-axis: the point (0, b).
a is the slope: when x increases by 1, y changes by a. If a > 0 the line rises; if a < 0 it falls.
Lines with the same a (same slope) are parallel.

example.q: Draw the graph of y = 2x + 1 using x = 0, 1, 2.
steps: Plot and join: a rising straight line cutting the y-axis at (0, 1); y goes up by 2 for each step of 1 in x

learn.reallife: A plot of distance against time for a train moving at steady speed is a straight line; the steeper the line, the faster the train.

games.title: Which point is on which line?
Line talk
items: The graph of y = 5x − 1 is a straight line
Every linear polynomial has a straight-line graph.
The line y = −3x + 2 rises from left to right
The slope −3 is negative, so the line falls as x increases.
The line y = 4x + 7 cuts the y-axis at (0, 7)
You need at least five points to draw the graph of a linear polynomial
Two points fix a straight line; a third is only a check.
The lines y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 3 are parallel
Both have slope 2, so they rise at the same rate and never meet.

quiz.q: What does the graph of y = 4x − 3 look like?
quiz.explain: y = 4x − 3 is a linear polynomial, and every linear polynomial has a straight-line graph.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a negative constant bends the graph

quiz.q: Where does the line y = 3x + 5 cut the y-axis?
quiz.explain: On the y-axis x = 0, so y = 3 × 0 + 5 = 5. The point is (0, 5).
quiz.mistake: Writes the intercept as (5, 0), swapping x and y

quiz.q: For y = 2x − 1, what is y when x = 4?
quiz.explain: Substitute x = 4: 2 × 4 − 1 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of subtracting it

quiz.q: Which line falls as x increases?
quiz.explain: A line falls when its slope (the coefficient of x) is negative. Only y = −3x + 1 has a negative slope.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the sign of the constant term instead of the coefficient of x

quiz.q: On the graph of y = 5x + 2, by how much does y increase when x goes up by 1?
quiz.explain: The coefficient of x is the slope. Each step of 1 in x adds 5 to y.
quiz.mistake: Chooses the constant term instead of the slope

quiz.q: Which point lies on the line y = −2x + 6?
quiz.explain: Check each point: for x = 1, y = −2 + 6 = 4, so (1, 4) is on the line.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the minus sign on the slope

quiz.q: Kabir has ₹100 and saves ₹20 every week, so his savings after x weeks are y = 20x + 100. After how many weeks will he have ₹260?
quiz.mistake: Divides 260 by 20 without removing the starting ₹100

quiz.q: A line passes through (0, 1) and (2, 7). Which equation does it show?
quiz.explain: It cuts the y-axis at 1, so b = 1. From x = 0 to x = 2, y rises by 6, so the slope is 6 ÷ 2 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Uses the total rise 6 as the slope without dividing by the run 2

teach.ask: Gappu has graph paper and a ruler: "How do I draw y = 2x + 1? Do I have to plot hundreds of points?"
teach.praise: Make a small table, plot two or three points and join them with a ruler. A perfect straight line!
teach.nudge: How many points do I really need, and what shape will I get?

learn.hook: A lemonade stall makes a loss at first and a profit later. The exact moment it breaks even is a zero of a polynomial!
points: A zero of p(x) is a value of x that makes p(x) = 0.
For p(x) = ax + b with a ≠ 0, solve ax + b = 0 to get the zero x = −b/a.
A linear polynomial has exactly one zero.
On the graph, the zero is where the line crosses the x-axis: the point (−b/a, 0).
To check a zero, substitute it: the answer must come out as 0.

example.q: Find the zero of p(x) = 3x − 12 and say where its graph meets the x-axis.
steps: The line meets the x-axis at (4, 0)
example.answer: x = 4; the graph crosses the x-axis at (4, 0)

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers find the break-even number of items, where profit is exactly zero, by finding the zero of a profit polynomial.

games.title: Match each polynomial with its zero

quiz.q: What is the zero of p(x) = x − 6?
quiz.explain: x − 6 = 0 gives x = 6. Check: 6 − 6 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Takes the constant with its sign (−6) as the zero

quiz.q: Find the zero of 4x + 20.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that moving +20 across makes it −20

quiz.q: Where does the graph of y = 2x − 10 cross the x-axis?
quiz.explain: On the x-axis y = 0, so 2x − 10 = 0 and x = 5. The crossing point is (5, 0).
quiz.mistake: Gives the y-intercept (0, −10) instead of the x-axis crossing

quiz.q: How many zeros does a linear polynomial ax + b (with a ≠ 0) have?
quiz.explain: A non-horizontal straight line crosses the x-axis exactly once, at x = −b/a.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up linear polynomials with quadratics, which can have two zeros

quiz.q: Is x = 3 a zero of p(x) = 3x − 9?
quiz.explain: p(3) = 3 × 3 − 9 = 0, so 3 is a zero.
quiz.mistake: Substitutes x = 0 instead of x = 3

quiz.q: Arjun's lemonade stall makes a profit of p(x) = 5x − 150 rupees when he sells x glasses. How many glasses must he sell to break even (zero profit)?
quiz.explain: Break even means p(x) = 0: 5x = 150, so x = 30.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts or multiplies instead of dividing 150 by 5

quiz.q: The zero of 3x + k is 2. What is k?
quiz.explain: Since 2 is a zero, 3 × 2 + k = 0, so k = −6.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the sign and writes k = 6

quiz.q: What is the zero of p(x) = 2x + 3?
quiz.mistake: Divides the wrong way round (−2/3) or loses the minus sign

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: "What is a 'zero' of a polynomial? Is it just the number 0?"
teach.praise: Oh! It is the x that makes the polynomial equal zero, where the line crosses the x-axis. Tweet-tastic!
teach.nudge: Is the zero a value of x or a value of p(x)? And where can I see it on the graph?
